last_reply:
The app is now a native Windows desktop player, with the same Audacity-following behaviour, layout, themes, file browser, fullscreen mode and keep-on-top option as the original. It builds cleanly and is packaged as a ready-to-run Windows program with its video decoder included, so there is nothing else to install.

All three automatic checks pass: the build succeeds, the app draws a real 1120×720 picture, and the recorded timing and layout values match the originals. I also produced a real 64-bit Windows program without a console window and corrected the target program’s fingerprint in the notes.

The one remaining unknown is how it behaves on an actual Windows machine: the connection to Audacity’s timecode display could not be exercised here, so that needs a Windows 10 or 11 test with Audacity 4.0.2. The next useful step is to run the packaged version alongside Audacity and confirm the timecode dot turns green.
